_drafted_from_note: Transcribed from the photograph, replacing an uncorrected EasyOCR draft. The page prints no chords at all, so by Robert's rule the pen is the answer here. Every chord is handwritten in red marker directly over the printed glyphs; the columns below were measured rather than eyeballed - the marker is red and the type black, so a colour threshold gives each chord its own bounding box, and the recogniser's word boxes give the lyric geometry to interpolate onto. TWO THINGS NEED A HUMAN EYE. (1) The exact syllable is not always recoverable: a marker letter is 35-45 px of scrawl on 21 px type, so read each chord as +/- one character. (2) Both `Hm` marks have a second, red mark to their LEFT that may be the same chord written and abandoned, or a crossed-out different one - `mert minden az enyem` at x 474-548 and `tudom az angyalok` at x 405-492. Each `Hm` is placed where its own surviving ink is, not where the red mark is; if the red mark is the intended position, move it left by about 6 characters. The right column carries no chords, which the manifest confirms. - assistant, 2026-08-25
